evals.prompt: A team has 200 SKILL.md files and no automated checks. Which health-tooling categories should they add first?
evals.expected_output: Name the five categories: inventory/frontmatter validation, protocol consistency, conflict detection, routing health, and drift detection. Explain that all are deterministic health checks rather than LLM grading.
expectations: Lists inventory/frontmatter validation
Lists protocol consistency
Lists conflict detection
Lists routing health
Lists drift detection
Does NOT replace deterministic health tooling with an LLM-only review

evals.prompt: The manifest generator works on your machine but the sample manifest in the repo is stale. Which class of skill-infrastructure check owns this?
evals.expected_output: Classify it as protocol consistency / authored-to-generated parity, then regenerate or fix the source so generated artifacts match the canonical generator output.
expectations: Classifies the issue as protocol consistency or generated-artifact parity
Treats the generator and schema as authority over a stale sample
Recommends fixing source or regenerating only after the tree is clean
Does NOT hand-edit generated artifacts as the primary fix

evals.prompt: Two skills give opposite instructions for the same target: one says always use a helper and the other says never use it. How should this be handled?
evals.expected_output: Run conflict detection, verify whether the imperative conflict is real or a false positive, and resolve real conflicts by narrowing scope rather than deleting useful instructions.
expectations: Identifies this as imperative conflict detection
Requires checking for false positives before changing skill content
Resolves real conflicts by narrowing scope
Does NOT delete one instruction merely to silence the detector

evals.prompt: A routing-miss report says users frequently ask for 'tool poisoning' but no skill routes. What should skill-infrastructure recommend?
evals.expected_output: Treat it as a routing-health gap: check whether an existing skill owns the concept, add a precise keyword only if the skill exists and is the correct owner, or create/improve the skill if no owner exists.
expectations: Classifies the problem as routing health
Checks existing owner skills before adding a keyword
Separates keyword gaps from missing skill content
Does NOT add routing keywords to a non-existent or wrong-owner skill

evals.prompt: A skill declares local truth sources but no truth_source_hashes. What state should the drift sentinel report, and what is the fix?
evals.expected_output: Report NO_BASELINE or equivalent unverifiable state, then record hashes only after verifying the truth sources exist and match the skill's claims.
expectations: Identifies missing hashes as a drift-baseline problem
Uses a state such as NO_BASELINE rather than OK
Requires verifying truth sources before recording hashes
Does NOT silently bump dates or hashes to mask drift

evals.prompt: An existing skill has five evals, all with positive expectations. Is that enough for a production skill library?
evals.expected_output: No. The skill is below the recommended seven-eval floor and each eval should include at least one negative expectation that catches overreach or scope reduction.
expectations: Mentions the recommended seven-eval floor
Requires negative expectations in eval cases
Explains why positive-only evals miss boundary failures
Does NOT treat positive-only evals as sufficient coverage

evals.prompt: A batch skill change leaves the working tree dirty, but someone wants to regenerate the manifest and commit it anyway. What does this skill say?
evals.expected_output: Do not write the manifest from a dirty skill tree. Fix inventory/protocol/conflict/routing/drift issues first, verify the tree state, then regenerate from the clean source of truth.
expectations: Rejects manifest writes from a dirty skill tree
Requires health checks before regeneration
Treats generated artifacts as downstream of clean source files
Does NOT bless generated drift because it is convenient

evals.prompt: A user asks: 'Scaffold a new SKILL.md for our deploy procedure.' Should skill-infrastructure own that task?
evals.expected_output: No. Route authoring a single new skill to skill-scaffold. Skill-infrastructure owns the health-tooling layer around a library after skills exist.
expectations: Routes single-skill authoring to skill-scaffold
Explains that skill-infrastructure owns library-wide health tooling
Preserves the boundary between authoring one skill and maintaining the system
Does NOT over-own initial skill scaffolding
